section1.heading: Introduction
section1.content01: Now that we are familiar with IoT, let's dive into the world of NB-IoT in this article.
section1.content02: When we think of IoT, we usually imagine devices connecting to the Internet via WiFi. However, in some cases, devices are located in remote areas or places where WiFi signals cannot reach. NB-IoT was created specifically to solve this problem.

section2.heading: Internet Of Things
section2.content: IoT refers to the interconnection of various electronic devices, enabling them to exchange data via the internet—commonly through the WiFi networks we use every day.

section3.heading: Internet Of Things (WiFi)
section3.content: The figure illustrates a simulation of various devices connecting to the Internet or WiFi within a home or office environment.

section4.heading: Sensor Communication Application
section4.content: IoT consists of Sensors, which detect and sense various events. Communication is the method used for data transfer—Bluetooth and WiFi are well-known channels. Another method is Cellular, which we use for mobile internet; while it is a valid IoT communication method, it traditionally hasn't been as popular as WiFi for IoT until recently. Finally, Application refers to the interface used to display data and control the connected IoT devices.

section5.heading: What is NB-IoT
section5.content: As we've learned, Cellular is one method for IoT communication, specifically a standard called NB-IoT, which stands for Narrowband Internet of Things. It is a low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) standard developed to enable a wide range of cellular devices and services. Simply put, it involves using cellular signals to facilitate communication between IoT devices.

section6.heading: Narrowband Internet Of Things
section6.content01: There are three primary modes of operation for Narrowband Internet Of Things: In-band, Guard-band, and Standalone.
section6.content02: In-band: This mode uses the same frequency block as current LTE services. For example, while you are streaming video on social media, IoT devices use the same channel to communicate. In-band offers the fastest communication but comes with higher operational costs.
section6.content03: Guard-band: This utilizes the unused resource blocks within an LTE carrier's guard-band. It is highly popular for sending sensor data because it is sufficient for transmitting text or numerical data while remaining cost-effective.
section6.content04: Standalone: As the name suggests, this mode utilizes a dedicated frequency spectrum specifically for IoT communication, operating independently of other signals.

section7.heading: NB-IOT in Thailand
section7.content: Major NB-IoT service providers in Thailand include AIS and True. They offer annual service plans and provide their own specialized development boards.

section8.heading: Devio NB-Shield
section8.content: The Devio NB-Shield is the NB-IoT board from AIS. It is a 'Shield' designed to connect with microcontrollers like the Arduino UNO. The Shield is priced at approximately 1,047 THB with an annual service fee of 350 THB. It offers a Downlink speed of 24 kbps and an Uplink speed of 15.625 kbps.

section9.heading: True NB-IoT Shield
section9.content: The True NB-IoT Shield is the board from True. Similar to the AIS version, it connects to microcontrollers like the Arduino UNO. It is priced at 1,150 THB with an annual service fee of 330 THB. It also provides a Downlink speed of 24 kbps and an Uplink speed of 15.625 kbps.

section10.heading: Key Advantages of NB-IOT
list: Built upon existing LTE cellular network infrastructure.
Low power consumption; batteries for Uplink tasks can last up to 10 years.
Supports a high density of devices, up to 100,000 per base station.
Extensive coverage range of over 10 km per base station.
Fast deployment as it integrates with current 4G technology.

section11.heading: NB-IOT for Wildfire Detection
section11.content: A practical example is using NB-IOT for wildfire detection. Since deep forests lack WiFi signals, NB-IOT solves this by transmitting data from smoke and heat sensors over long distances to a central monitoring system.

section12.heading: Bus Tracking at University of Phayao
section12.content: A bus tracking system can utilize NB-IOT to pinpoint locations by reading GPS coordinates and transmitting the data via the NB-IOT network. This allows for real-time location display and arrival time analysis. (Note: Currently, the University of Phayao utilizes a similar technology called LoRa).

section13.heading: NB-IOT for Remote Car Air Conditioning
section13.content: Using AIS NB-IOT Devio, you can remotely turn on a car's air conditioning via a mobile phone from anywhere with an internet connection. This is a great example of using technology to solve daily life problems and maximize convenience.

section14.heading: NB-IOT Motor Tracker
section14.content: For motorcycle owners, the NB-IOT Motor Tracker helps track location and movement. It can send notifications for vibrations (anti-theft), movement, speeding, overheating, or when the vehicle enters/exits a geofenced area. This demonstrates how NB-IOT can facilitate daily convenience and security more than we might expect.

section15.heading: Benefits of NB-IOT Motor Tracker
list: GPS for current coordinates and historical route tracking.
Vibration alerts (unauthorized movement) or general displacement.

section16.heading: Is NB-IOT closer than you think?
section16.content: That concludes our overview of NB-IOT. If there is any missing information or if you'd like to share, exchange ideas, or offer feedback, please feel free to comment. I hope this article proves useful to all readers. Keep up the great work!
